content.text:
Connect Jira to Cursor through the **official Atlassian MCP plugin**. After it is linked, Agent chat can search, read, create, and update Jira work items using your existing Jira permissions.

### Recommended: Cursor Marketplace

1. Open the [Atlassian plugin for Cursor](https://cursor.com/marketplace) (search **Atlassian**).
2. Select **Add to Cursor**.
3. When Cursor prompts you, complete the Atlassian **OAuth** login and approve Jira (and Confluence if you want that too).
4. Confirm the server is connected in **Cursor Settings → MCP**.

You need an **Atlassian Cloud** site (for example `yourcompany.atlassian.net`). This is not installed from Jira’s “Manage apps” screen; it is installed the first time someone on the site completes the OAuth consent.

### Alternative: add the MCP server yourself

In MCP settings (or `.cursor/mcp.json`), point at Atlassian’s v2 server:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "atlassian": {
      "url": "https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

Then sign in when Cursor starts the Atlassian auth flow.

Official setup: [Get started with the Atlassian MCP server](https://support.atlassian.com/atlassian-ai-gateway/docs/get-started-with-the-atlassian-remote-mcp-server/).

### After it is connected

In a new Agent chat, try:

- “What’s the status of PROJ-1234?”
- “List my open Jira issues.”
- “Create a Jira bug from this stack trace.”

If auth was previously stale, **Disconnect** the Atlassian MCP entry, fully quit Cursor, then **Connect** again.

This workspace has no Jira MCP configured yet (`mcpServers` is empty). If you want, I can start the plugin install from here so you only need to confirm in the tray and sign in.

content.text:
Yes. That prompt is choosing **where the MCP config is saved**, not which Jira site to use.

| Choice | Saved to | Who sees it |
|---|---|---|
| **User** | `C:\Users\Hariprasanth_Baskara\.cursor\mcp.json` | You, in **every** Cursor project |
| **Workspace** | `.cursor/mcp.json` in this folder (`c:\Users\Hariprasanth_Baskara\cursor`) | Only this project (and teammates if you commit that file) |

**For Jira / Atlassian, pick User.** It is your personal OAuth login, you will want it in all repos, and you should not commit credentials into the project.

Use **Workspace** only if the whole team should share the same *server definition* for this repo (URL/command), not your personal token. Cursor merges both files; if the same server name exists in both, **workspace wins**.

After you pick a scope, finish Connect / OAuth as usual.

content.text:
The GitHub JSON is only a URL. Cursor never finished login, so the handshake stays `auth=unknown` and the connection fails.

Your current entry in `C:\Users\Hariprasanth_Baskara\.cursor\mcp.json` is:

```json
"github": {
  "url": "https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/"
}
```

That hosted GitHub MCP **does not complete OAuth in Cursor**. GitHub does not support Dynamic Client Registration, so Cursor cannot finish auth from the URL alone. Official GitHub docs for Cursor say you need a **Personal Access Token**.

### Fix

1. Create a token at [https://github.com/settings/tokens](https://github.com/settings/tokens) (classic) or [fine-grained tokens](https://github.com/settings/personal-access-tokens/new).
   - Typical scopes: `repo`, `read:org`, `read:user` (add more if you need issues/PRs/workflow).
2. Replace the `github` block with:

```json
"github": {
  "url": "https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/",
  "headers": {
    "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_GITHUB_PAT"
  }
}
```

3. Save the file, fully quit Cursor, reopen it.
4. In **Settings → MCP**, confirm `github` shows a green/connected status.

Do not paste the token into chat.

### If it still fails with the same `connect_failure`

Cursor has a known bug: it can ignore `headers` and try OAuth anyway when GitHub advertises OAuth discovery. Then use the **local** server with the token in `env` (not headers):

```json
"github": {
  "command": "docker",
  "args": [
    "run",
    "-i",
    "--rm",
    "-e",
    "GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN",
    "ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server"
  ],
  "env": {
    "GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN": "YOUR_GITHUB_PAT"
  }
}
```

Docker Desktop must be running.

After it connects, try: “List my GitHub repositories.”
I'll check whether Cursor Marketplace has an official GitHub plugin you can install instead of editing JSON.

content.text:
Yes. Cursor has a first-party **GitHub** marketplace plugin, and it includes the GitHub MCP server.

- Plugin: [cursor.com/marketplace/cursor/github](https://cursor.com/marketplace/cursor/github)
- MCP entry: [cursor.com/marketplace/mcp/github](https://cursor.com/marketplace/mcp/github)

**Install from Cursor**

1. Open **Customize** in the sidebar.
2. Open **MCPs** (or Plugins).
3. Search **GitHub**.
4. Click **Add to Cursor**.
5. Complete GitHub sign-in when prompted.

That is cleaner than a hand-written `mcp.json` URL. After it is installed, check **Settings → MCP** for a green/connected `github` status.

Your current JSON-only `https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/` entry can stay disabled or be removed so it does not fight the plugin.

If you want, I can open the install confirm tray from here.
